title: E2E default-branch and protected Production promotion classification

phases.objective: Classify trusted default-branch execution, declared parallel pull requests, and the exact protected main-to-Production promotion without inheriting unrelated pull-request environment state or weakening fail-closed branch rules.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: The parallel PR flow self-test invokes the canonical E2E PR gate in isolated synthetic Git contexts.
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Default-branch/manual execution is classified as standard, declared workstreams retain their bounded mode, undeclared PR branches fail closed, and only exact same-repository main-to-Production identity is accepted as a protected promotion.
steps: Create a synthetic repository baseline and bind a local origin/main ref.
Remove inherited pull-request base/head environment variables for the default-branch fixture.
Invoke the canonical gate for main without a PR base ref and require standard mode.
Invoke the gate for an undeclared branch with an Integration base and require a bounded rejection.
Retain direct workstream-to-main rejection and valid declared workstream classification.
Retain exact main-to-Production acceptance and spoofed promotion rejection.
assertions: Default-branch/manual execution does not inherit enclosing pull-request identity.
The undeclared-branch guard is enforced only when a pull-request base ref exists.
Declared workstream and Integration branch rules remain fail closed.
Merge-queue refs remain excluded from ordinary PR classification.
Only exact protected main-to-Production identity is treated as a Production promotion.
No repository write, protected-ref update, deployment, provider call, credential read, SQL, migration Apply, database mutation, or external send occurs.

phases.objective: Observe the classifier across protected pull requests, workflow dispatches, and default-branch runs using canonical structured E2E evidence.
Retain bounded diagnostics for inherited environment variables, missing refs, spoofed promotion identities, stale SHAs, and malformed parallel-work contracts.
Validate one non-production default-branch/manual run and one declared parallel pull-request flow before relying on the classification in later protected promotion cycles.
Require the exact classifier and self-test evidence for every protected main-to-Production promotion without granting merge or deployment authority.
